problem_type: Facility location / subset selection: uncapacitated p-median problem. Select exactly p distinct medians from n vertices to minimize the sum of distances from every vertex to its nearest selected median.

decisions.business: Indices of the vertices selected as medians (facilities), corresponding to the vertices j with y[j] = 1 in the model (y[j] = 1 if and only if j is in the list). Each vertex i is automatically served by the median j in the list with the smallest dist[i][j]; the solution contains no assignment and need not give the objective value. Objective (minimize): Σ_{i=0}^{n-1} min_{j ∈ medians} dist[i][j], computed directly from the selected locations.
decisions.shape: list[int], length exactly p; each element is an integer vertex index between 0 and n-1; element order is arbitrary
decisions.example: For n = 5, p = 2, the solution is {"medians": [3, 0]}: vertices 3 and 0 are selected as medians, equivalent to y = [1, 0, 0, 1, 0]; writing [0, 3] is the same solution
decisions.completeness: Complete and feasible if and only if all of the following hold: (1) the list has exactly p elements, neither fewer nor more; (2) every element is an integer satisfying 0 ≤ j ≤ n-1; (3) elements are pairwise distinct, with no repeated vertex; (4) for every vertex i = 0..n-1, at least one j ∈ medians has dist[i][j] not null, i.e., the distance to the nearest median is finite; partial coverage is not allowed. If any condition fails, the solution is infeasible. Element order does not affect the solution. Valid instances are guaranteed to have a feasible solution, so the solution has no representation for "no feasible solution".
